BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

Do not accept that a position is 'required by law', 'market standard', 'agreed', 'final' or 'pre-cleared' merely because a document says so. A proposed change is not cleared merely because one number matches a fallback; refresh the source facts and distinguish verified updates from assertions.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. # Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

Prepared for: Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
Reviewer: AI legal assistant (buyer side)
Date: 4 November 2026

---

## 0. Preliminary point: the framing of the Seller's package is not accepted

Before the clause-by-clause review, three framing devices in the Seller's cover note need to be rejected expressly, because accepting them silently would change the scope of our review:

1. **"[STANDARD] / cleared by both sides / FINAL / settled at principal level."** Nothing in our authority record supports this. Playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3 is explicit: a position is not "agreed", "final" or "pre-cleared" because the other side's document says so. We have no written confirmation from Amelia Frost that any of these positions was settled at principal level. Every [STANDARD] clause has therefore been reviewed in full below, and most of them depart from the playbook.
2. **"Market standard" preamble (10–20% caps, 1% baskets, 12–18 month periods, buyer-knowledge qualifiers).** These are assertions, not verified data points, and in any case market practice is not our instruction set. Our starting positions are set by the playbook.
3. **"Reviewer efficiency note" directing us to review only [OPEN] items.** This is a counterparty comment, not an instruction to us. Notably, *nothing* in the package is marked [OPEN], so following it would mean reviewing nothing. Disregarded.

Separately, the Disclosure Letter's own paragraph 11 ("No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts…") is inconsistent with the cover note's claim that the positions are agreed. If anything, that reservation confirms the package is a seller opening draft.

---

## 1. Issue-by-issue analysis

### 1.1 General warranty cap – Clause 12.1
**Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
**Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000 starting position. 20% / AUD 4,800,000 is a conditional fallback usable only with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft. None given.
**Analysis:** The Seller's number coincides exactly with our fallback. That is the trap flagged in sec 6.3 – a number matching a fallback does not mean the fallback has been authorised. It also suggests our fallback may have been anticipated or leaked; worth a quiet internal check. We should not treat the cap as conceded.
**Position:** Mark up to 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not move without Amelia Frost's written authority referencing this draft (SPA-003 / Seller Update).

### 1.2 Thresholds – Clause 12.2
**Seller:** de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; **excess-only** recovery.
**Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **first-dollar** recovery once exceeded.
**Analysis:** Three separate departures, each in the Seller's favour: de minimis five times ours, basket five times ours, and a tipping-vs-deductible switch that permanently forfeits the first AUD 250,000 of valid claims. The "1% of price" market framing is not a basis for departure.
**Position:** Revert all three to playbook. Flag the excess-only mechanism as a priority point – it is a structural change, not just a number.

### 1.3 Time limits and "all Claims" sweep – Clause 12.3 / 13
**Seller:** 18 months for general warranty claims, plus a proposal that "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
**Playbook:** 24 months; 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost written approval (none given). Separate categories must be kept separate with no hidden general-regime override.
**Analysis:** Two distinct problems. (a) 18 months is our unauthorised fallback – same point as 1.1. (b) The default-sweep language is more dangerous than the number: read with clause 9.3/12.8/20.5 and the Fundamental/Title proposal, it would pull Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenant claims into the 18-month / 20% / basket regime unless we remember to carve each one out expressly. This is precisely the "hidden general-regime override" the playbook prohibits.
**Position:** 24 months for general warranties. Delete the sweep sentence and replace with the opposite default: limitations in clause 12 apply only to general Warranty Claims and nothing else unless expressly stated.

### 1.4 Fundamental / Title warranties
**Seller:** Same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
**Playbook:** Separate regime – 100% of price cap, at least six years, outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
**Analysis:** "Administrative simplicity" is not a commercial justification for capping title and capacity exposure at 20% and 18 months. If title to the shares fails, the loss is the whole price.
**Position:** Insert a Fundamental Warranty regime per playbook. Non-negotiable in substance.

### 1.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature" – Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5
**Seller:** Applies to all Claims of any nature.
**Playbook:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must be carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the maximum extent enforceable; no one may waive this. Categories kept separate.
**Analysis:** As drafted there is **no fraud carve-out anywhere in the package**. "All Claims of any nature" would purport to cap and time-bar fraud and to exclude reliance on fraudulent statements. Enforceability aside, this is the single clearest departure from a non-waivable playbook position and must be fixed before any other trading occurs.
**Position:** Insert an express fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct carve-out applying across clauses 8, 9, 12, 13 and 20. Confine 12.8 and 20.5 to general Warranty Claims; preserve specific indemnities, covenant claims and title claims as separate remedies.

### 1.6 Disclosure framework – Schedule 7 and Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.2
**Seller:** Whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012) as at 22 September 2026, plus Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" deemed disclosed.
**Playbook:** Specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
**Analysis:** Para 1.1 and 1.2 are exactly the general-disclosure model we reject. Combined with clause 8.3 (below), the effect would be that almost nothing in the warranties is claimable. Note also para 1.4 – the Seller makes no admission of anything – which is acceptable boilerplate in itself but reinforces that the specific disclosures in paras 2–10 are descriptive only and do not quantify or accept any exposure.
**Position:** Delete paras 1.1–1.2. Disclosure to be effective only if fairly and specifically disclosed in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Data room documents may be referenced, but only where the Letter expressly identifies the relevant document and the matter it discloses.

### 1.7 Buyer knowledge exclusion – Clause 8.3
**Seller:** No claim for any matter the Buyer *or its advisers* knew of, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
**Playbook:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier requires named seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry (i.e. seller-side knowledge, not buyer-side), and never applies to title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
**Analysis:** This is a constructive-knowledge bar extended to advisers and to anything "discoverable". It converts the warranties into a due-diligence-at-buyer's-risk model and would effectively make the DD findings (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006 etc.) unclaimable. It also overlaps with 1.6 to double-lock the warranty package.
**Position:** Delete clause 8.3. If any knowledge concept survives, it is a seller-knowledge qualifier on specified warranties only, by reference to named individuals after reasonable enquiry.

### 1.8 Bluefen consent – Clause 3 / 6.3; Disclosure Letter para 2
**Seller:** Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.
**Disclosure:** Bluefen ≈ AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30%); consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3; **no final written consent and no evidence that the 11.3 conditions are satisfied** as at the Letter date.
**Playbook:** Require effective consent AND evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a material customer.
**Analysis:** The Seller's own disclosure confirms the condition is unsatisfied on its own terms and that the consent is conditional (11.3). A consent-on-delivery condition would let a conditional or ineffective consent satisfy the CP. For a customer representing ~30% of revenue this is a value-critical point.
**Position:** CP to require (a) written consent from Bluefen in agreed form, unconditional or with all 11.3 conditions satisfied and evidenced, (b) no termination/re-pricing notice, and (c) Seller to use all reasonable endeavours (or best endeavours) with buyer approval of the consent form. Status is "outstanding" – not "addressed".

### 1.9 Riverlark facility – Clause 2 / 7; Disclosure Letter para 3
**Seller:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion."
**Disclosure:** Not repaid; no final discharge of security in the data room; change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2 in DD-003.
**Playbook:** Current payout letter; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective security releases at Completion. A post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking plus Amelia Frost approval.
**Analysis:** On a debt-free/cash-free deal, completing with AUD 3.2m of secured debt outstanding and no release in hand means we would be paying full price and acquiring a secured company, relying on the Seller to procure a release afterwards. The change-of-control provision (8.1) also raises a risk of default on Completion absent lender consent.
**Position:** Completion deliverables to include a current payout letter, Riverlark's consent/waiver under 8.1, repayment directed from the Completion funds flow, and executed releases/PPSR discharges at Completion. Playbook sec: no post-completion release unless irrevocable lender undertaking + Amelia Frost written approval. Neither exists.

### 1.10 Employee bonuses – Funds flow; Disclosure Letter para 5
**Seller:** AUD 420,000 DD-005 completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow.
**Disclosure:** Bonuses conditional on Completion and continued employment; **not in the funds flow**; silent on payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs.
**Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or demonstrably seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
**Analysis:** "A matter for the Seller" is not a mechanism. Once Completion occurs the bonuses crystallise as an obligation of the Company (our company) unless the funds flow deducts them or the Seller funds them with an enforceable undertaking. The on-costs (super, payroll tax, possibly leave loading) are unquantified and could add a meaningful percentage on top.
**Position:** Either (a) specific deduction line in the funds flow for AUD 420,000 plus a calculated on-cost amount, or (b) Seller-funded with an express covenant and indemnity. Request the on-cost calculation now. Treat as Transaction Expense / Debt-like item in the price mechanics.

### 1.11 Ironquay IP – Clause 11.1; Disclosure Letter para 4
**Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate."
**Disclosure:** DD-004 cl 7.3 makes transfer of SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open but this is **not independent bank verification**; no receipt and no confirmatory assignment in the data room.
**Playbook:** Broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
**Analysis:** The real exposure is not the AUD 180,000 – it is that title to the SOW3 Project Materials may not have passed to the Company at all. A payment-only indemnity does not cover loss of IP ownership, third-party claims, re-development cost or the need to re-procure. The Seller's disclosure confirms the gap it says is adequately covered.
**Position:** Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own the SOW3 (and other Ironquay) deliverables, uncapped by the general regime. Require as a pre-Completion step: evidence of cleared payment (bank record, not DD-010) and a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay. Keep the SOW3 cure route (pay and obtain assignment) available, funded by the Seller.

### 1.12 Export / privacy incident – Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6; Disclosure Letter para 6
**Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material."
**Disclosure:** Download link sent to an unintended external address; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps); unknown whether accessed, exact scope unknown, notification requirement undetermined; investigation preliminary; not characterised as a confirmed breach; no loss amount.
**Playbook:** Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
**Analysis:** The Seller's "not expected to be material" is an opinion, not a finding. Equally, we should not overstate it. The correct approach is process-based: this is a known, unresolved matter that could crystallise before or after Completion.
**Position:** (a) Pre-Completion covenant: preserve all access/download logs, continue the investigation, provide written updates and the final report before Completion; (b) specific indemnity for loss arising from the DD-006 incident (regulatory, notification, third-party claims), outside the general cap/basket; (c) no price adjustment proposed at this stage; (d) ensure the general disclosure of DD-006 does not neutralise the privacy/data warranties.

### 1.13 Sandbar supplier renewals – Disclosure Letter para 8
**Seller:** Ordinary-course operating costs.
**Disclosure:** Three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000); DD-008 and DD-011 to be read together for timing/scope; silent on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
**Playbook:** Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
**Analysis:** The Seller asserts "ordinary course" but its own disclosure disclaims that characterisation. Need to establish: renewal dates relative to Completion, whether any is already committed/accrued, termination rights, and whether the three are a single package. If any amount is committed pre-Completion but payable post, it may be a working-capital or debt-like item.
**Position:** Do not accept the Seller's characterisation; do not yet assert a deduction. Raise DD follow-up questions. Treat as open pending answers.

### 1.14 Tax / IP – "settled under the general regime"
**Seller:** Settled under the general regime.
**Playbook:** Tax and IP terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution; keep categories separate.
**Analysis:** "Settled" is an assertion. Nothing has been agreed. Rolling Tax and IP into the general regime would subject them to the 20% / 18-month / AUD 250k-basket package, which is inconsistent with the separate-categories requirement and with the specific Ironquay exposure.
**Position:** Mark Tax and IP as OPEN. Propose separate Tax warranty/indemnity regime (longer period, separate cap) and separate IP regime; do not propose unlimited liability. Reject the "settled" label.

### 1.15 Title – Disclosure Letter para 10
**Seller:** Title evidenced by the share register at DD-012.
**Disclosure:** DD-012 identifies the source the Seller relies on; "does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification."
**Playbook:** Independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence required; DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
**Analysis:** The Seller's own letter concedes the register is only the source it relies on. A company-maintained register is not independent evidence against encumbrances, PPSR registrations, Riverlark security over shares, or authority.
**Position:** Completion deliverables / DD: ASIC current extract, PPSR search against the Company and the Seller, Riverlark confirmation that no share security remains, Seller board/shareholder authorisations, officer's certificate. Fundamental warranties on title and capacity per 1.4.

### 1.16 Other disclosures (lease, Mossvale) – paras 7 and 9
Office lease (DD-007) is a notification obligation only; Mossvale (DD-009) is an assignment restriction not triggered by a share sale. Both appear low-risk on the disclosed facts, but we should confirm by reading the underlying clauses ourselves rather than relying on the Seller's characterisation, and add the lease notification as a pre- or post-Completion covenant.

---

## 2. Interaction effects – why the package is worse than its parts

Read together, clauses 8.3 (buyer/adviser knowledge, incl. "discoverable"), Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.2 (whole data room + public records), 12.3/13 (all-claims sweep), 9.3/12.8/20.5 (limitations to all claims of any nature) and the Fundamental/Title proposal produce the following result: every matter in the data room – including all the known problems (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, DD-006) – is deemed disclosed and known, therefore unclaimable; anything not in the data room is capped at 20%, subject to a AUD 250k excess-only basket, barred after 18 months, and (on the Seller's drafting) this would extend to title, tax, IP, specific indemnities and fraud. This is not a "fair and balanced package"; it is a near-complete exclusion of seller liability.

---

## 3. Summary of recommendations

| # | Item | Seller draft | Our mark-up | Authority status |
|---|------|-------------|-------------|------------------|
| 1 | Framing ([STANDARD]/FINAL/efficiency note) | Treat as agreed | Reject; full review; no clause is cleared | Playbook 0.4/6.3 |
| 2 | Cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m | Fallback not authorised – Amelia Frost written authority needed before any move |
| 3 | Thresholds (12.2) | AUD 25k / AUD 250k / excess-only | AUD 5k / AUD 50k / first-dollar | Playbook |
| 4 | Time limit (12.3) | 18 months + all-claims sweep | 24 months; delete sweep; limitations apply to general warranties only | 18m fallback not authorised |
| 5 | Fundamental/Title | Same as general | 100% cap, 6+ years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge | Playbook – firm |
| 6 | Fraud carve-out (9.3/12.8/20.5) | None; all claims of any nature | Express carve-out from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy, non-reliance | Non-waivable |
| 7 | Disclosure (Sch 7, DL 1.1–1.2) | Whole data room + public records | Specific fair disclosure only | Playbook – firm |
| 8 | Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Blanket, incl. advisers and "discoverable" | Delete; any qualifier is seller-knowledge, named persons, reasonable enquiry; never title/capacity/fraud/indemnities | Playbook – firm |
| 9 | Bluefen (3/6.3) | Reasonable endeavours; consent-on-delivery | Effective consent + evidence 11.3 conditions satisfied, pre-Completion | Playbook; currently unsatisfied per DL para 2 |
| 10 | Riverlark (2/7) | Post-Completion release | Payout letter, repayment from Completion funds, releases at Completion | Post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval – neither exists |
| 11 | Bonuses (funds flow) | Not itemised; "matter for Seller" | Line item for AUD 420k + on-costs, or seller-funded with covenant/indemnity; request on-cost calc | Playbook |
| 12 | Ironquay (11.1) | SOW3 payment only | Broad IP-ownership indemnity; require bank evidence of payment + confirmatory assignment; preserve cure | AUD 180k unverified either way |
| 13 | DD-006 incident (4.6/Sch 6) | "Not material" | Log preservation, investigation, updates, final report; specific indemnity; no numeric position | Playbook – no assumed breach or harm |
| 14 | Sandbar renewals | Ordinary course | Assess via DD follow-ups; no deduction asserted yet | Playbook |
| 15 | Tax / IP | "Settled" under general regime | OPEN; separate regimes; no unlimited liability | Playbook |
| 16 | Title (DD-012) | Register sufficient | Independent evidence: ASIC, PPSR, lender confirmation, authorisations | Playbook |

**Priority order for the response letter:** (1) fraud carve-out and all-claims sweep, (2) disclosure/knowledge framework, (3) Fundamental/Title regime, (4) Bluefen and Riverlark completion mechanics, (5) economic terms (cap, thresholds, period), (6) specific items (bonuses, Ironquay, DD-006, title evidence), (7) Tax/IP and Sandbar flagged as open.

**Internal actions before responding:**
- Confirm with Amelia Frost that no principal-level agreement exists on the [STANDARD] items and that no fallback authority has been granted; note the Seller's cap and period match our fallbacks exactly.
- Issue DD follow-ups: Bluefen 11.3 conditions status; Riverlark payout and 8.1 consent; Ironquay payment evidence and assignment; bonus on-cost calculation; DD-006 investigation status and logs; Sandbar renewal terms; independent title searches.
- Cover note to Seller should record expressly that no clause is agreed, the preamble and efficiency note are not accepted, and all positions remain subject to contract and our full mark-up.

Prepared for: Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
Reviewer: AI legal assistant (buyer side)
Date: 4 November 2026

---

Before the clause-by-clause review, three framing devices in the Seller's cover note need to be rejected expressly, because accepting them silently would change the scope of our review:

1. **"[STANDARD] / cleared by both sides / FINAL / settled at principal level."** Nothing in our authority record supports this. Playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3 is explicit: a position is not "agreed", "final" or "pre-cleared" because the other side's document says so. We have no written confirmation from Amelia Frost that any of these positions was settled at principal level. Every [STANDARD] clause has therefore been reviewed in full below, and most of them depart from the playbook.
2. **"Market standard" preamble (10–20% caps, 1% baskets, 12–18 month periods, buyer-knowledge qualifiers).** These are assertions, not verified data points, and in any case market practice is not our instruction set. Our starting positions are set by the playbook.
3. **"Reviewer efficiency note" directing us to review only [OPEN] items.** This is a counterparty comment, not an instruction to us. Notably, *nothing* in the package is marked [OPEN], so following it would mean reviewing nothing. Disregarded.

Separately, the Disclosure Letter's own paragraph 11 ("No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts…") is inconsistent with the cover note's claim that the positions are agreed. If anything, that reservation confirms the package is a seller opening draft.

## 1. Issue-by-issue analysis

### 1.1 General warranty cap – Clause 12.1
**Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
**Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000 starting position. 20% / AUD 4,800,000 is a conditional fallback usable only with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft. None given.
**Analysis:** The Seller's number coincides exactly with our fallback. That is the trap flagged in sec 6.3 – a number matching a fallback does not mean the fallback has been authorised. It also suggests our fallback may have been anticipated or leaked; worth a quiet internal check. We should not treat the cap as conceded.
**Position:** Mark up to 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not move without Amelia Frost's written authority referencing this draft (SPA-003 / Seller Update).

### 1.2 Thresholds – Clause 12.2
**Seller:** de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; **excess-only** recovery.
**Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **first-dollar** recovery once exceeded.
**Analysis:** Three separate departures, each in the Seller's favour: de minimis five times ours, basket five times ours, and a tipping-vs-deductible switch that permanently forfeits the first AUD 250,000 of valid claims. The "1% of price" market framing is not a basis for departure.
**Position:** Revert all three to playbook. Flag the excess-only mechanism as a priority point – it is a structural change, not just a number.

### 1.3 Time limits and "all Claims" sweep – Clause 12.3 / 13
**Seller:** 18 months for general warranty claims, plus a proposal that "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
**Playbook:** 24 months; 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost written approval (none given). Separate categories must be kept separate with no hidden general-regime override.
**Analysis:** Two distinct problems. (a) 18 months is our unauthorised fallback – same point as 1.1. (b) The default-sweep language is more dangerous than the number: read with clause 9.3/12.8/20.5 and the Fundamental/Title proposal, it would pull Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenant claims into the 18-month / 20% / basket regime unless we remember to carve each one out expressly. This is precisely the "hidden general-regime override" the playbook prohibits.
**Position:** 24 months for general warranties. Delete the sweep sentence and replace with the opposite default: limitations in clause 12 apply only to general Warranty Claims and nothing else unless expressly stated.

### 1.4 Fundamental / Title warranties
**Seller:** Same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
**Playbook:** Separate regime – 100% of price cap, at least six years, outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
**Analysis:** "Administrative simplicity" is not a commercial justification for capping title and capacity exposure at 20% and 18 months. If title to the shares fails, the loss is the whole price.
**Position:** Insert a Fundamental Warranty regime per playbook. Non-negotiable in substance.

### 1.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature" – Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5
**Seller:** Applies to all Claims of any nature.
**Playbook:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must be carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the maximum extent enforceable; no one may waive this. Categories kept separate.
**Analysis:** As drafted there is **no fraud carve-out anywhere in the package**. "All Claims of any nature" would purport to cap and time-bar fraud and to exclude reliance on fraudulent statements. Enforceability aside, this is the single clearest departure from a non-waivable playbook position and must be fixed before any other trading occurs.
**Position:** Insert an express fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct carve-out applying across clauses 8, 9, 12, 13 and 20. Confine 12.8 and 20.5 to general Warranty Claims; preserve specific indemnities, covenant claims and title claims as separate remedies.

### 1.6 Disclosure framework – Schedule 7 and Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.2
**Seller:** Whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012) as at 22 September 2026, plus Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" deemed disclosed.
**Playbook:** Specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
**Analysis:** Para 1.1 and 1.2 are exactly the general-disclosure model we reject. Combined with clause 8.3 (below), the effect would be that almost nothing in the warranties is claimable. Note also para 1.4 – the Seller makes no admission of anything – which is acceptable boilerplate in itself but reinforces that the specific disclosures in paras 2–10 are descriptive only and do not quantify or accept any exposure.
**Position:** Delete paras 1.1–1.2. Disclosure to be effective only if fairly and specifically disclosed in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Data room documents may be referenced, but only where the Letter expressly identifies the relevant document and the matter it discloses.

### 1.7 Buyer knowledge exclusion – Clause 8.3
**Seller:** No claim for any matter the Buyer *or its advisers* knew of, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
**Playbook:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier requires named seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry (i.e. seller-side knowledge, not buyer-side), and never applies to title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
**Analysis:** This is a constructive-knowledge bar extended to advisers and to anything "discoverable". It converts the warranties into a due-diligence-at-buyer's-risk model and would effectively make the DD findings (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006 etc.) unclaimable. It also overlaps with 1.6 to double-lock the warranty package.
**Position:** Delete clause 8.3. If any knowledge concept survives, it is a seller-knowledge qualifier on specified warranties only, by reference to named individuals after reasonable enquiry.

### 1.8 Bluefen consent – Clause 3 / 6.3; Disclosure Letter para 2
**Seller:** Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.
**Disclosure:** Bluefen ≈ AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30%); consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3; **no final written consent and no evidence that the 11.3 conditions are satisfied** as at the Letter date.
**Playbook:** Require effective consent AND evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a material customer.
**Analysis:** The Seller's own disclosure confirms the condition is unsatisfied on its own terms and that the consent is conditional (11.3). A consent-on-delivery condition would let a conditional or ineffective consent satisfy the CP. For a customer representing ~30% of revenue this is a value-critical point.
**Position:** CP to require (a) written consent from Bluefen in agreed form, unconditional or with all 11.3 conditions satisfied and evidenced, (b) no termination/re-pricing notice, and (c) Seller to use all reasonable endeavours (or best endeavours) with buyer approval of the consent form. Status is "outstanding" – not "addressed".

### 1.9 Riverlark facility – Clause 2 / 7; Disclosure Letter para 3
**Seller:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion."
**Disclosure:** Not repaid; no final discharge of security in the data room; change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2 in DD-003.
**Playbook:** Current payout letter; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective security releases at Completion. A post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking plus Amelia Frost approval.
**Analysis:** On a debt-free/cash-free deal, completing with AUD 3.2m of secured debt outstanding and no release in hand means we would be paying full price and acquiring a secured company, relying on the Seller to procure a release afterwards. The change-of-control provision (8.1) also raises a risk of default on Completion absent lender consent.
**Position:** Completion deliverables to include a current payout letter, Riverlark's consent/waiver under 8.1, repayment directed from the Completion funds flow, and executed releases/PPSR discharges at Completion. Playbook sec: no post-completion release unless irrevocable lender undertaking + Amelia Frost written approval. Neither exists.

### 1.10 Employee bonuses – Funds flow; Disclosure Letter para 5
**Seller:** AUD 420,000 DD-005 completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow.
**Disclosure:** Bonuses conditional on Completion and continued employment; **not in the funds flow**; silent on payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs.
**Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or demonstrably seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
**Analysis:** "A matter for the Seller" is not a mechanism. Once Completion occurs the bonuses crystallise as an obligation of the Company (our company) unless the funds flow deducts them or the Seller funds them with an enforceable undertaking. The on-costs (super, payroll tax, possibly leave loading) are unquantified and could add a meaningful percentage on top.
**Position:** Either (a) specific deduction line in the funds flow for AUD 420,000 plus a calculated on-cost amount, or (b) Seller-funded with an express covenant and indemnity. Request the on-cost calculation now. Treat as Transaction Expense / Debt-like item in the price mechanics.

### 1.11 Ironquay IP – Clause 11.1; Disclosure Letter para 4
**Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate."
**Disclosure:** DD-004 cl 7.3 makes transfer of SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open but this is **not independent bank verification**; no receipt and no confirmatory assignment in the data room.
**Playbook:** Broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
**Analysis:** The real exposure is not the AUD 180,000 – it is that title to the SOW3 Project Materials may not have passed to the Company at all. A payment-only indemnity does not cover loss of IP ownership, third-party claims, re-development cost or the need to re-procure. The Seller's disclosure confirms the gap it says is adequately covered.
**Position:** Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own the SOW3 (and other Ironquay) deliverables, uncapped by the general regime. Require as a pre-Completion step: evidence of cleared payment (bank record, not DD-010) and a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay. Keep the SOW3 cure route (pay and obtain assignment) available, funded by the Seller.

### 1.12 Export / privacy incident – Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6; Disclosure Letter para 6
**Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material."
**Disclosure:** Download link sent to an unintended external address; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps); unknown whether accessed, exact scope unknown, notification requirement undetermined; investigation preliminary; not characterised as a confirmed breach; no loss amount.
**Playbook:** Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
**Analysis:** The Seller's "not expected to be material" is an opinion, not a finding. Equally, we should not overstate it. The correct approach is process-based: this is a known, unresolved matter that could crystallise before or after Completion.
**Position:** (a) Pre-Completion covenant: preserve all access/download logs, continue the investigation, provide written updates and the final report before Completion; (b) specific indemnity for loss arising from the DD-006 incident (regulatory, notification, third-party claims), outside the general cap/basket; (c) no price adjustment proposed at this stage; (d) ensure the general disclosure of DD-006 does not neutralise the privacy/data warranties.

### 1.13 Sandbar supplier renewals – Disclosure Letter para 8
**Seller:** Ordinary-course operating costs.
**Disclosure:** Three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000); DD-008 and DD-011 to be read together for timing/scope; silent on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
**Playbook:** Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
**Analysis:** The Seller asserts "ordinary course" but its own disclosure disclaims that characterisation. Need to establish: renewal dates relative to Completion, whether any is already committed/accrued, termination rights, and whether the three are a single package. If any amount is committed pre-Completion but payable post, it may be a working-capital or debt-like item.
**Position:** Do not accept the Seller's characterisation; do not yet assert a deduction. Raise DD follow-up questions. Treat as open pending answers.

### 1.14 Tax / IP – "settled under the general regime"
**Seller:** Settled under the general regime.
**Playbook:** Tax and IP terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution; keep categories separate.
**Analysis:** "Settled" is an assertion. Nothing has been agreed. Rolling Tax and IP into the general regime would subject them to the 20% / 18-month / AUD 250k-basket package, which is inconsistent with the separate-categories requirement and with the specific Ironquay exposure.
**Position:** Mark Tax and IP as OPEN. Propose separate Tax warranty/indemnity regime (longer period, separate cap) and separate IP regime; do not propose unlimited liability. Reject the "settled" label.

### 1.15 Title – Disclosure Letter para 10
**Seller:** Title evidenced by the share register at DD-012.
**Disclosure:** DD-012 identifies the source the Seller relies on; "does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification."
**Playbook:** Independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence required; DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
**Analysis:** The Seller's own letter concedes the register is only the source it relies on. A company-maintained register is not independent evidence against encumbrances, PPSR registrations, Riverlark security over shares, or authority.
**Position:** Completion deliverables / DD: ASIC current extract, PPSR search against the Company and the Seller, Riverlark confirmation that no share security remains, Seller board/shareholder authorisations, officer's certificate. Fundamental warranties on title and capacity per 1.4.

### 1.16 Other disclosures (lease, Mossvale) – paras 7 and 9
Office lease (DD-007) is a notification obligation only; Mossvale (DD-009) is an assignment restriction not triggered by a share sale. Both appear low-risk on the disclosed facts, but we should confirm by reading the underlying clauses ourselves rather than relying on the Seller's characterisation, and add the lease notification as a pre- or post-Completion covenant.

## 2. Interaction effects – why the package is worse than its parts

Read together, clauses 8.3 (buyer/adviser knowledge, incl. "discoverable"), Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.2 (whole data room + public records), 12.3/13 (all-claims sweep), 9.3/12.8/20.5 (limitations to all claims of any nature) and the Fundamental/Title proposal produce the following result: every matter in the data room – including all the known problems (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, DD-006) – is deemed disclosed and known, therefore unclaimable; anything not in the data room is capped at 20%, subject to a AUD 250k excess-only basket, barred after 18 months, and (on the Seller's drafting) this would extend to title, tax, IP, specific indemnities and fraud. This is not a "fair and balanced package"; it is a near-complete exclusion of seller liability.
